options: Codes for the names of countries, territories and special areas of geographical interest
questions.explanation: ISO 3166 is an international standard that defines codes for the names of countries, territories and special areas of geographical interest.

questions.stem: What type of data is ISO 3166 described as?
questions.explanation: ISO 3166 is described as one type of Reference Data.

questions.stem: What are the three types of ISO 3166-1 codes?
questions.explanation: ISO 3166-1 provides Alpha-2 two-letter codes, Alpha-3 three-letter codes and three-digit Numeric codes for each country or territory.

questions.stem: What is the ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3 code for Canada?
questions.explanation: Canada's codes are Alpha-2 CA, Alpha-3 CAN and Numeric 124.

questions.stem: What is the ISO 3166-1 Numeric code for the United States?
questions.explanation: The United States has Alpha-2 code US, Alpha-3 code USA and Numeric code 840.

questions.stem: Who maintains ISO 3166 and why is it periodically updated?
options: The International Organization for Standardization, to reflect changes in country names and geopolitical developments
The Basel Committee, to reflect changes in banking regulation
The Bank for International Settlements, to track currencies
Each national government, to record its own borders
questions.explanation: The standard is maintained by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and is periodically updated to reflect changes in country names and geopolitical developments.

questions.stem: How are ISO 3166 codes used in database integration?
options: To uniquely identify countries and ensure consistency in data representation
To replace primary keys in every table
To store the full text of treaties
questions.explanation: ISO 3166 codes are commonly used in databases and information systems to uniquely identify countries, ensuring consistency in data representation.

questions.stem: Why does using ISO 3166 codes instead of full country names improve efficiency?
options: Because codes are easier to translate
Because codes make data entry and processing more efficient
Because codes are required by every database
questions.explanation: The use of codes instead of full country names makes data entry and processing more efficient.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an application of ISO 3166 codes?
options: Data exchange between systems and organisations
Specifying the countries involved in trade and finance
questions.explanation: ISO 3166 codes are used for database integration, international transactions and data exchange; bank capital adequacy is a Basel matter.

questions.stem: In the game analogy for ISO 3166, what role do the agreed codes play?
options: They decide who wins the game
They keep score for each player
They translate the rules into every language
They make sure everyone knows which country is being referred to, no matter where they are from
questions.explanation: ISO 3166 is like a set of agreed rules for using simple codes so that everyone knows which country is being referred to, no matter where they are from.
